rules.rule: Check for urgent urinary symptom conditions

rules.problem: Nothing is checked for the right-hand branch of the page: blood on dipstick with Schistosoma ova on microscopy / bilharzia risk, which the page resolves to 'Schistosomiasis likely'. The check_for list matches the left-hand branch faithfully.
Structure and trigger match the red box; only the diagnosis concept loses the 'complicated' qualifier (see c043).

The page puts 'uncomplicated pyelonephritis likely' under 'not needing urgent attention', i.e. flank pain with leucocytes/nitrites and none of the complicating features (vomiting, BP < 90/60, pulse ≥ 100, diabetes, male, pregnant, post menopause). The rule has no exclusion of those features, so it also fires for every complicated case. Because both rules diagnose the same concept the practical effect is small, but the rule is not faithful to the page's branching.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable simple UTI in a woman (urinary symptoms)

rules.problem: Both branches (woman with a complicating factor; man without prostatitis features, with leucocytes/nitrites and frequency/urgency) follow the page. Diagnosis concept is broader than the page (see c083).

rules.rule: Diagnose probable male urethritis syndrome (urinary symptoms)
Diagnose possible diabetes (urinary symptoms with glycosuria)
rules.problem: 'exclude diabetes' correctly rendered as a possible diagnosis; the woman and man paths both match the page.

rules.rule: Urgent: urinary symptoms with danger signs
rules.problem: Urgent is justified by the 'Give urgent attention' heading; and/or structure follows the four red-box bullets, with kidney disease and kidney stone via active_condition and complicated pyelonephritis inlined (unavoidable, since its concept is shared with the uncomplicated rule).

summary: No invented or misplaced content: every condition traces to the page in the right rule and role, and the Urgent priority rule mirrors the red box. The main gap is coverage, not distortion: the page's 'Schistosomiasis likely' (blood on dipstick, Schistosoma ova positive or bilharzia risk without microscopy) has no probable rule and nothing is checked for it. Two concept choices are lossy because SNOMED lacks the qualified disorders: complicated and uncomplicated pyelonephritis both become 'Acute pyelonephritis', and 'Complicated UTI' becomes the parent 'Urinary tract infectious disease' that also covers the Simple UTI concept; the uncomplicated pyelonephritis rule also omits the exclusion of the complicating features that the page implies.
